description: Nusa Nova is a student-led team from Indonesia, inspired by the spirit of Nusantara and the possibilities of space exploration. We combine curiosity, science, and creative design to turn NASA’s open data into accessible tools for exploring other worlds. Our mission is to help people understand complex challenges, make informed decisions, and imagine humanity’s future beyond Earth.
summary: HOMEBOUND combines NASA Mars imagery, terrain and regional context to show how much observation time fits after outward travel, return travel and reserve are counted. Users compare changes and export a source-linked mission brief, connecting an image-supported science question to a decision they can explain.
details:
THE QUESTION

How much science fits when the return is already counted?

An interesting observation point on Mars is only part of a plan. Outward travel, observation, the journey home and protected reserve all use the same time budget. HOMEBOUND makes that complete-trip trade-off visible before departure.

WHAT HOMEBOUND DOES

HOMEBOUND is a browser-based, return-aware Marswalk planning prototype for a roughly 1.52 km-wide study area within Gale Crater. It integrates NASA optical imagery, terrain and broader regional context in a four-step workflow: Destination, Activities, Review and Save brief.

Users choose one destination, declare their observation and travel assumptions, inspect the modeled round trip, and compare a revised observation with the original plan. They can export a PDF, text or JSON brief containing the result, assumptions, map context and source references.

SCIENCE CONNECTED TO A DECISION

At Site S, a marked HiRISE image shows dark linear patterns beside a brighter, rough-textured patch. This motivates an investigation into how the visible texture transition relates to local relief.

Under Science walkthrough, the budget is 120 minutes and the protected reserve is 20 minutes. A 20-minute observation fits. Extending it to 88 minutes exceeds the budget by 0.40 minutes. Reducing it to 85 minutes makes the plan fit again, leaving 2.60 minutes of extra margin without consuming the reserve.

The apps explains the consequence of the user's choice; it does not automatically prescribe an optimal observation duration.

EXPLAINABLE ASSUMPTIONS

Terrain elevation and slope support directional travel-time estimates and shortest-path searches. Optical imagery supports the science question; THEMIS provides qualitative context, while Mars Trek/MOLA shows the regional setting.

Science walkthrough uses a 20-degree slope limit and 120-minute budget. Terrain exploration tests 30 degrees and 180 minutes for original A/B/C. These presets use the same data and model, with different explicit assumptions. The higher slope is an exploration assumption, not validated walking guidance.

IMPLEMENTATION AND VALUE

HOMEBOUND runs in a web browser. Its calculations and key features were checked using automated tests, checks with NASA data, and browser-based testing.

HOMEBOUND's focus is complete-trip time accounting, explainable what-if comparison and a science-to-brief workflow. It helps users see what fits, understand why a change matters, and share the evidence behind the decision.
